subject: muzzleflash1
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: sprites/muzzleflash1.spr, in the place of the game's own

R1.reason: Both frames show a five-pointed star burst with a bright white-hot core and thin rays fading outward, which is the muzzle flash the brief describes. Nothing in either frame reads as another effect.

R2.reason: Each frame is 64 x 64, as measured. The star fills most of each frame with a margin of dark around it, and the rays reach toward the edges without being clipped. Both frames are the same size and centred.

R3.reason: By eye the colours are a white-yellow core with orange-amber rays on a near-black ground, which is how a bright additive flash should blend. Both frames carry the same palette, with no colour cast.

R4.reason: Two frames, as the class's measures ask. Border is 0.02 max and 0 mean (dark, so the flash does not spill over the edge), and first (0.95) and last (1.0) frames are both at or above the 0.9 bar for a muzzle flash. Frame 1 is a bright flash of its own with slightly different ray angles rather than a fade to dark, so there is no motion fault.

R5.reason: The measured type and format match the original's: parallel and additive for both the replacement and the game's file. It keeps the same name (sameName true) and reads back as written (readsBack true). There is no fault in the kept block.
